sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The front matter of the English WHO recommendations on optimizing health worker roles to improve access to key maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting (OptimizeMNH, 2012), with cataloguing data, ISBN and copyright. It also includes the table of contents. It lists annexes such as the frameworks for each cadre, the GRADE evidence base and a workbook for contextualizing the guidelines.

sections.title: Definitions of cadres included in the OptimizeMNH guidance

summary.text: A table defining the health worker cadres included in the OptimizeMNH guidance, from advanced level associate clinicians and associate clinicians to auxiliary nurses, auxiliary nurse midwives, lay health workers, midwives, nurses and non-specialist doctors. For each it describes training, competencies and regulation and lists alternative titles used in different countries. Footnotes note that only trained traditional birth attendants were considered and that the WHO definition of midwife was used.

sections.extract: Definitiona Different names Advanced level associate clinicianb A professional clinician with advanced competencies to diagnose and manage the most common medical, maternal, child health and surgical conditions, including obstetric and gynaecological surgery (e.g. caesarian sections). Advanced level associate clinicians are generally trained for 4 to 5 years post-secondary education in established higher education

sections.title: Executive summary

summary.text: Opens the executive summary, stating that health workforce shortages threaten the health-related MDGs and that redistributing tasks among cadres, including mid-level and lay workers, is a promising way to improve access and cost-effectiveness. It notes the need to define which maternal and newborn interventions different cadres can deliver safely and effectively.

sections.extract: Human resource shortages in the health services are widely acknowledged as a threat to the attainment of the health- related Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). Attempts to optimize the potential of the existing health workforce are therefore crucial. A more rational distribution of tasks and responsibilities among cadres of health workers is seen as a promising strategy for improving access and cost- effectiveness

sections.title: Objectives

summary.text: States that the guidance aims to provide evidence-based recommendations for universal access to key maternal and newborn interventions by optimizing health worker roles, for policy-makers and managers who will adapt them to their national context.

sections.extract: These recommendations have been developed as part of the World Health Organization’s mandate to provide normative guidance to its member states. The objective of this guidance is to issue evidence-based recommendations to facilitate universal access to key, effective maternal and newborn interventions through the optimization of health worker roles. These recommendations are intended for health policy- makers,

sections.title: Guidance development methods

summary.text: Describes how the guidance was developed following the WHO handbook, using GRADE evidence profiles from systematic reviews complemented by qualitative and programme evidence. It explains the four categories of recommendation, from recommending the option to recommending against it, including options suggested only in rigorous research.

sections.extract: The procedures used in the development of this guidance are outlined in the WHO handbook for guideline development (1). These are: (i) the identification of questions related to practice and health policy for which answers are needed; (ii) the retrieval of up-to-date research-based evidence; (iii) the assessment and synthesis of evidence; (iv) the formulation of recommendations with inputs from a wide range of

sections.title: Recommendations

summary.text: Reports that an international Guidance Panel approved the recommendations at meetings in Geneva in April and June 2012, making 119 recommendations across cadres, from 36 for lay health workers to 1 for non-specialist doctors. It notes one excluded question on misoprostol self-administration and the removal of antiretroviral recommendations to align with other WHO guidelines.

sections.extract: and approved by an international group of experts (the Guidance Panel) who participated in the WHO Technical Consultation on Optimizing the Delivery of Key Interventions to Attain MDGs 4 and 5 (OptimizeMNH) meeting held in Geneva, Switzerland from 16–19 April 2012 and on 26 June 2012. The experts also identified important knowledge gaps that need to be addressed through further primary research. Recommendations The

sections.title: Dissemination, adaptation and implementation of the recommendations

summary.text: Stresses that implementation will depend on health system and sociocultural contexts and calls for national dialogue on whether shortages of skilled workers limit access and which cadres and intervention packages are suitable for task shifting. It advises treating individual recommendations as packages by condition and cadre.

sections.extract: implementation of the recommendations The Guidance Panel acknowledged that health system arrangements and specific sociocultural and political factors will shape the implementation of the recommendations in specific contexts. National dialogue is therefore needed, including discussions regarding whether the (non)availability of skilled health workers is a significant contributor to the accessibility and utilization

sections.title: Overview of judgements

summary.text: Lists the practices recommended by the Guidance Panel for each cadre, beginning with promotional and some clinical interventions for lay health workers, such as promoting antenatal care, birth preparedness, nutrition and family planning. It continues through auxiliary nurses, nurses, midwives and associate clinicians, covering tasks such as administering uterotonics, magnesium sulphate and caesarean sections by advanced level associate clinicians. It ends with external cephalic version by non-specialist doctors with targeted monitoring and evaluation.

sections.extract: The practices recommended by the Guidance Panel are listed below. The full list (which includes practices recommended only in the context of rigorous research as well as practices not recommended by the Guidance Panel) is presented in Chapter 4 (‘Evidence and recommendations’). sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces task shifting, or task sharing, as training cadres to take on tasks they did not previously perform in order to improve access and health system performance, noting that terms are used loosely. It places the guidance within WHO's GREAT project for developing evidence-based guidelines and supporting their adaptation and implementation.

sections.extract: Many WHO Member States have attempted to increase access to effective interventions. One way of facilitating improvement is to give available cadres short periods of additional training and then to allow them to take on particular activities they have not undertaken before. This process is known as ‘task shifting’ or ‘task sharing’ and is one of several strategies that can potentially improve the utilization of

sections.title: The global health workforce crisis

summary.text: Describes the global health workforce crisis, noting that 57 countries face severe shortages, 36 of them in sub-Saharan Africa, which bears 24% of the global disease burden with 3% of the health workforce. It also highlights rural–urban imbalances and shortages of specialist doctors.

sections.extract: Widespread crises in the health workforce are impacting on the realization of the health-related MDGs. According to a 2006 World Health Report, 57 countries face chronic human resource shortages in the health sector. Typically, such countries are LMICs and are nations with the highest burden of health problems such as HIV/AIDS and maternal and newborn mortality (3). Such problems are compounded by global and

sections.title: Human resource gaps in maternal and newborn health

summary.text: Uses skilled birth attendance to illustrate staffing gaps in maternal and newborn health, noting that about 52 million births a year occur without a skilled attendant and coverage is below 50% in much of South Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. It contrasts this with the high skilled attendance and physician density of countries with the lowest maternal and neonatal mortality.

sections.extract: newborn health The low proportion of women assisted by skilled birth attendants is an important indicator of the global personnel shortage in the health sector. Approximately 60 million births each year occur in settings other than health facilities and 52 million of these births take place without the support of a skilled birth attendant (5). While skilled birth attendance is provided at almost all births in most

sections.title: Optimizing the roles of health workers through task shifting: Overarching principles

summary.text: Sets out the overarching principles of WHO guidance on optimizing health worker roles through task shifting to improve access to maternal and newborn health interventions. It notes progress on skilled birth attendance since the MDGs and describes how some countries have trained lay health workers, defined as workers with intervention-specific training but no formal professional qualification. It places such programmes within the WHO health systems building blocks, shown in Figure 1.

sections.extract: through task shifting: Overarching principles National health strategies help to facilitate both improved levels of access and good quality care. Following the global endorsement of the MDGs, further efforts have been made in low- and middle-income countries to improve maternal and newborn health by improving levels of skilled birth attendance and institutional birth coverage. sections.title: Methods

summary.text: Summarises how the guidance was developed under WHO guideline procedures and the GREAT project, from identifying critical questions to grading evidence, formulating recommendations and planning dissemination.

sections.extract: This guidance represents the WHO’s efforts to support the use of evidence-informed policies and practices in all countries. The guidance forms part of the WHO’s Knowledge-to-Action GREAT project (10). This guidance was developed using standardized operating procedures in accordance with the processes described in the WHO handbook for guideline development (1) and draws on the methods described in the Handbook for

sections.title: Identification of critical questions and critical outcomes

summary.text: Describes how the need for the guidance was assessed through an online prioritization survey with 393 responses, most from low- and middle-income countries, and through requests from Member States, for example about lay health workers giving misoprostol. It explains how critical questions and outcomes were defined for each health worker cadre. It clarifies that changes requiring training that effectively creates a different cadre were not treated as task shifting.

sections.extract: critical outcomes The following steps were performed in order to identify critical questions and outcomes for the guidance: Assessment of the need for guidance The need for guidance was assessed in two ways: a) A WHO guidance prioritization survey: An online survey was conducted to identify WHO guidance priorities for maternal and perinatal health. A survey was sent to WHO regional and country offices as well as to

sections.title: Retrieval of the evidence

summary.text: Describes the three types of evidence used: effectiveness studies of delivery by specific cadres, qualitative studies of implementation factors, and country case studies of scaling up health workforces. Cochrane systematic reviews were the main effectiveness source, with outdated reviews updated by their authors. A cross-cutting analysis of implementation factors was structured by the WHO health systems building blocks.

sections.extract: Three main types of evidence were considered: • Evidence on the effectiveness of the delivery of interventions by specific cadres based on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized controlled trials (n-RCTs), controlled before-and-after studies (CBAs), interrupted time series studies (ITS), and cohort studies. • Evidence based on qualitative studies of factors affecting the implementation of programmes to

sections.title: Assessment, synthesis and grading of the evidence

summary.text: Explains how data were extracted from the effectiveness reviews and rated using GRADE as high, moderate, low or very low certainty, with reasons for downgrading such as bias, inconsistency and indirectness. It describes how confidence in the qualitative evidence was assessed. It notes that the country case study findings could not be formally graded because they drew on very diverse sources.

sections.extract: evidence Evidence on the effectiveness of the delivery of interventions by specific health workers Relevant information and data were extracted in a consistent manner from each of the systematic reviews of effectiveness by applying the following procedures: firstly, the up-to-date review documents and/or data were obtained from the review authors or the Cochrane Library. Secondly, analyses relevant to the critical

sections.title: Presentation of the evidence in a structured health systems framework

summary.text: Explains that evidence for each question was presented using the DECIDE evidence-to-recommendations framework, developed with the GRADE Working Group to support health system decisions. The framework recorded criteria, judgements, research evidence and other considerations, supported by evidence profiles and qualitative summaries in the annexes.

sections.extract: structured health systems framework In this guidance, evidence for each question is presented using the ‘Developing and Evaluating Communication Strategies to Support Informed Decisions and Practice Based on Evidence’ framework (also known as the DECIDE evidence-to-recommendations framework). This framework was developed as part of the DECIDE6 project in association 6 Further information about the DECIDE project can

sections.title: Formulation of recommendations

summary.text: Describes how recommendations were finalized at two technical consultations in 2012, the second dealing only with contraception. It notes that recommendations on antiretrovirals for preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission were removed to align with newer WHO HIV guidelines. It explains how the panel weighed desirable and undesirable consequences, reached decisions, and revised recommendations after peer review.

sections.extract: The option recommendations were finalized during two separate technical consultations. At the first consultation (16–19 April 2012), all recommendations except those relating to contraceptives were completed, while the second consultation (26 June 2012) focused only on recommendations related to contraceptives. sections.title: Planning for dissemination, implementation, impact evaluation and updating

summary.text: Notes that implementation, dissemination and impact evaluation are covered in later chapters and that the recommendations will be updated by 2018 unless new evidence requires it.

sections.extract: implementation, impact evaluation and updating During the technical consultations, participants discussed how the guidance might be implemented (Chapter 6) and disseminated (Chapter 8), and how the impacts of the guidance might be evaluated (Chapter 9). The implementation was discussed in the context of an approach developed specifically for health systems guidance (24). The recommendations will be updated by 2018

sections.title: Evidence and recommendations

summary.text: Explains that the recommendations are presented by health worker category, with implementation considerations after each and general considerations in Box 1.

sections.extract: In the following sections, the recommendations and the justification and conditions regarding each question are presented according to each health worker category. The implementation considerations for each cadre are presented after each recommendation while the implementation considerations for all cadres in general are presented at the end of this chapter in Box 1.

sections.title: Interventions considered for lay health workers

summary.text: Presents the recommendations on tasks for lay health workers, covering promotion of maternal and newborn health behaviours, postpartum haemorrhage, supplements, labour support, sepsis, kangaroo mother care, neonatal resuscitation and contraception. It begins with the question of whether lay health workers should promote a long list of behaviours and services, from antenatal care and birth preparedness to breastfeeding and immunization. Each recommendation comes with a justification and conditions. The section ends with contraceptive delivery, stressing training on communication and side-effects and that lay health workers should not apply their own eligibility criteria.

sections.title: Interventions considered for auxiliary nurses

summary.text: Presents the recommendations for auxiliary nurses, covering postpartum haemorrhage, antibiotics for preterm pre-labour rupture of membranes, kangaroo mother care, neonatal sepsis and resuscitation, pregnancy and childbirth interventions and contraception. It recommends that auxiliary nurses give oxytocin by standard syringe to prevent postpartum haemorrhage, judging that benefits probably outweigh harms despite limited evidence. Each recommendation includes justification, conditions and implementation considerations. The section ends with a cross-reference list of related recommendations, such as continuous labour support and puerperal sepsis management.

summary.text: Presents the recommendations for auxiliary nurse midwives across postpartum haemorrhage, antibiotics for preterm pre-labour rupture of membranes, kangaroo mother care, neonatal care, pregnancy and childbirth interventions and contraception. It makes no recommendation on distributing misoprostol for self-administration, calling for more research while noting this may limit access. It goes on to consider whether they should diagnose preterm pre-labour rupture of membranes and give initial injectable antibiotics before referral. The section ends with cross-references to related recommendations, including maternal intrapartum care.

summary.text: Presents the recommendations for nurses on antibiotics for preterm pre-labour rupture of membranes, external cephalic version, specific pregnancy and childbirth interventions and contraception. It ends with general implementation considerations and cross-references to related recommendations.

sections.title: Interventions considered for associate clinicians (non-physician clinicians)

summary.text: Presents the recommendations for associate clinicians, or non-physician clinicians, on external cephalic version and specific pregnancy and childbirth interventions. It recommends against them performing external cephalic version or vacuum extraction because these fall outside their usual scope and evidence is lacking. It suggests considering a loading dose of magnesium sulphate before referral with targeted monitoring, and ends with cross-references to contraception recommendations.

sections.title: Interventions considered for advanced level associate clinicians (non-physician clinicians)

summary.text: Sets out the OptimizeMNH task-shifting recommendations for advanced level associate clinicians (non-physician clinicians), such as performing external cephalic version only within rigorous research and performing vacuum extraction. For each question it gives the recommendation, its justification and conditions, citing limited evidence but possible gains in equity. It lists general implementation issues and the many interventions accepted as within this cadre's competence without evidence review, including contraception and tubal ligation.

summary.text: Gives the task-shifting recommendation that non-specialist doctors may perform external cephalic version for breech at term with targeted monitoring and evaluation, citing low- to moderate-certainty evidence of benefits. It lists tasks accepted as within their competence without evidence review. It ends with implementation considerations on referral, supplies and incentives.

sections.title: Implementing task shifting programmes: a summary of key cross-cutting factors based on reviews of qualitative studies and country case studies

summary.text: Explains that the chapter on implementing task-shifting programmes draws on five reviews of qualitative studies and a study of stakeholder views on optimizing health worker roles.

sections.extract: cross-cutting factors based on reviews of qualitative studies and country case studies The findings summarized in this chapter are based on an analysis of five reviews exploring the factors affecting the implementation of task shifting initiatives (14-18) and on a study of stakeholder views on optimizing the roles of health- care providers (19)7.

sections.title: Governance and leadership

summary.text: Describes governance and leadership factors in task-shifting programmes, such as social values, political ideology and local autonomy, contrasting Brazil's Family Health Program with problems in India's ASHA programme. It also covers district management capacity and barriers to community involvement in programme implementation.

sections.extract: Societal beliefs and values may influence decisions to implement health programmes and the acceptance of such programmes locally. Similarly, political ideology may influence the way in which responsibility for health is divided across governmental tiers and the willingness of local governing parties to implement programmes with particular equity objectives. sections.title: Financing

summary.text: Notes financing challenges for task shifting, including unclear financial roles across levels of government and payment methods such as fee-for-service that may make physicians see task shifting as a threat to income.

sections.extract: The disbursement and management of funds: The challenges identified included a lack of clarity regarding the roles and financial responsibilities and authority of national and sub-national structures and a lack of knowledge and appropriate financial management guidelines at the local service level. Payment methods: The choice of payment method can affect provider motivation. It can also influence relationships among

sections.title: Access to commodities

summary.text: Notes that drug and supply shortages and poor transport can undermine task shifting, supervision and referrals.

sections.extract: Drug and supply shortages may negatively impact programme implementation and task shifting. Inadequate transport infrastructure may also affect the ability of health providers to reach clients, the ability of district officers to provide supervision to health providers, and the referral of patients to health facilities.

sections.title: Service delivery

summary.text: Describes how task shifting affects health workers' roles and identities, for example by disrupting continuity of care for midwives or raising lay health workers' status. It discusses providers' views, including role ambiguity, job satisfaction when supported and fear when training is lacking, and workload changes. It also covers recipients' views, noting that closer social distance can improve care but threaten confidentiality for stigmatized conditions.

sections.extract: The impact of task shifting on the roles and identities of health-care providers: Task shifting may result in changes to the meaning of particular provider roles within a broader organizational context, to working relationships, and to relations between different components of a health system. The shifting of more technological tasks to midwives, for instance, may disrupt the relationships between midwives and

sections.title: Health workforce

summary.text: Summarizes workforce issues in task shifting, including inadequate or poorly matched training and weak supervision, and suggests field-based supervision and peer support.

sections.extract: Pre-service and in-service training: Problems include the inadequate provision of training, training that does not address practice needs, unskilled trainers, inflexible training schedules, and unrealistic and unachievable training requirements. The reviews suggested that training needs to evolve in relation to changes in the roles of cadres or the tasks that they are expected to undertake. Supervision and support:

sections.title: Contextualizing guidance

summary.text: Explains how countries can adapt the OptimizeMNH task-shifting guidance using an eight-step framework for health systems guidance in policy-making. Steps include identifying the national policy venue and timing, clarifying the problem and options, and considering health system and political contexts. It describes combining global evidence with local data and views in evidence briefs for policy dialogues.

sections.extract: Using evidence-informed global guidance, such as recommendations issued by the WHO, can help countries to improve their health system performance. However, developing or changing health policies and health systems involves complex processes. Most guidance documents do not contextualize recommendations in relation to specific national needs, particularly with regard to health and political systems. This section

sections.title: Research implications

summary.text: Lists the Guidance Panel's observations on research needs, noting a worrying lack of reliable data on task shifting, especially for mid-level cadres such as auxiliary nurses and associate clinicians. It recommends qualitative research alongside effectiveness trials and evaluating packages of interventions and team models. It then poses specific research questions for each health worker cadre.

sections.extract: The following general observations regarding future research were made by the Guidance Panel during the meetings: • There was a general agreement that despite the attention given to task shifting and to lay health worker programmes in LMICs in particular, the paucity of reliable research data was alarming. • Most of the research evidence identified related to both barriers and facilitators and the effectiveness of

sections.title: Dissemination of the recommendations

summary.text: Describes plans to disseminate the task-shifting recommendations through WHO's Knowledge-to-Action framework, WHO offices, ministries, UN agencies and NGOs, the WHO Reproductive Health Library and a policy brief. It stresses participatory national adaptation. It lists priority dissemination actions such as piloting a workbook and using online channels.

sections.extract: The ultimate goal of these recommendations is to improve the quality of care and health outcomes for mothers and infants. The dissemination and implementation of this guidance are crucial steps which should be undertaken by the international community and national and local health care services. The WHO Department of Reproductive Health and Research has adopted a formal Knowledge-to-Action framework for the

sections.title: Review and updating of the recommendations

summary.text: Explains that feedback from adapting the task-shifting recommendations will inform updates, that evidence-to-recommendation frameworks are being user-tested, and that the guidance will be updated by 2018 unless new evidence requires earlier change.

sections.extract: The recommendations included in this guidance and the derivative products will be used in international and national adaptation initiatives. Feedback received will be recorded and used to contribute to future updates. Members of the WHO Technical Secretariat and researchers from The Norwegian Knowledge Centre for the Health Services are currently conducting user testing of the evidence-to-recommendation frameworks

narratives.es: Figura 1, los componentes básicos de los sistemas de salud de la OMS: seis círculos naranjas superpuestos con las etiquetas gobernanza, información, financiación, prestación de servicios, recursos humanos, y medicamentos y tecnologías, dispuestos alrededor de una zona central con la etiqueta «Personas». La imagen está recortada por el borde izquierdo, lo que trunca el título y el texto.
narratives.fr: Figure 1, les éléments constitutifs des systèmes de santé selon l'OMS : six cercles orange qui se chevauchent, intitulés gouvernance, information, financement, prestation de services, ressources humaines, et médicaments et technologies, disposés autour d'une zone centrale intitulée « Personnes ». Le rendu est rogné sur le bord gauche, ce qui tronque le titre et le texte.
narratives.ru: Рисунок 1 — составные элементы систем здравоохранения ВОЗ: шесть пересекающихся оранжевых кругов с подписями «руководство», «информация», «финансирование», «оказание услуг», «кадровые ресурсы» и «лекарственные средства и технологии», расположенных вокруг центральной области с подписью «Люди». Изображение обрезано по левому краю, из-за чего заголовок и основной текст неполны.

narratives.en: Page render whose lower part is Figure 2, a shaded text box of selected opinions from stakeholders in the online discussion. Its three bullets state that most contributors agreed lay health workers could safely deliver promotional and behavioural interventions but agreed less on therapeutic ones such as injections; that appropriately trained and supervised traditional birth attendants can play an important role where serious service gaps exist; and that good planning and community–facility linkages are important for timely referral to higher levels of care.
narratives.ar: صورة صفحة يتضمن جزؤها السفلي الشكل 2، وهو مربع نصي مظلل يعرض آراء مختارة لأصحاب المصلحة في المناقشة الإلكترونية. وتفيد نقاطه الثلاث بأن معظم المشاركين اتفقوا على أن العاملين الصحيين غير المتخصصين يمكنهم تقديم التدخلات الترويجية والسلوكية بأمان، لكنهم كانوا أقل اتفاقاً بشأن التدخلات العلاجية مثل الحقن؛ وبأن القابلات التقليديات المدرّبات والخاضعات للإشراف على نحو مناسب يمكنهن أداء دور مهم حيث توجد فجوات خطيرة في الخدمات؛ وبأهمية التخطيط الجيد والروابط بين المجتمعات المحلية والمرافق لضمان الإحالة في الوقت المناسب إلى مستويات الرعاية الأعلى.
narratives.zh: 页面图像，下半部分为图2：一个带底色的文本框，列出在线讨论中利益攸关方的部分意见。三个要点指出：大多数参与者认为非专业卫生工作者可以安全地提供宣传和行为干预，但对注射等治疗性干预意见较不一致；在存在严重服务缺口的地方，经过适当培训和监督的传统助产士可以发挥重要作用；良好的规划以及社区与卫生机构之间的联系对于及时转诊至更高层级医疗服务十分重要。
narratives.es: Imagen de una página cuya parte inferior es la figura 2, un recuadro sombreado con opiniones seleccionadas de las partes interesadas en el debate en línea. Sus tres viñetas indican que la mayoría de los participantes coincidieron en que los trabajadores de salud legos podían prestar con seguridad intervenciones de promoción y conductuales, pero hubo menos acuerdo sobre las terapéuticas como las inyecciones; que las parteras tradicionales debidamente capacitadas y supervisadas pueden desempeñar un papel importante donde existen graves carencias de servicios; y que una buena planificación y los vínculos entre comunidades y establecimientos son importantes para la derivación oportuna a niveles superiores de atención.
narratives.fr: Rendu de page dont la partie inférieure est la figure 2, un encadré grisé présentant une sélection d'opinions des parties prenantes lors de la discussion en ligne. Ses trois puces indiquent que la plupart des contributeurs ont convenu que les agents de santé non professionnels pouvaient fournir en toute sécurité des interventions de promotion et comportementales, mais étaient moins d'accord pour les interventions thérapeutiques comme les injections ; que des accoucheuses traditionnelles correctement formées et supervisées peuvent jouer un rôle important là où existent de graves lacunes de services ; et qu'une bonne planification et des liens entre communautés et établissements sont importants pour l'orientation rapide vers des niveaux de soins supérieurs.
narratives.ru: Изображение страницы, в нижней части которой находится рисунок 2 — затенённый текстовый блок с избранными мнениями заинтересованных сторон из онлайн-обсуждения. В трёх пунктах говорится, что большинство участников согласились с тем, что непрофессиональные медицинские работники могут безопасно проводить просветительские и поведенческие мероприятия, но были менее единодушны в отношении лечебных вмешательств, например инъекций; что надлежащим образом подготовленные и контролируемые традиционные повитухи могут играть важную роль там, где имеются серьёзные пробелы в услугах; и что хорошее планирование и связи между общинами и учреждениями важны для своевременного направления на более высокие уровни помощи.

narratives.en: Figure 3, framework for evidence-based health systems guidance for policy-making: a vertical sequence of eight chevron-shaped steps in shades of orange, each with a grey text bar: clarify the problem; frame the options; identify implementation considerations; consider the broader health system context; consider the broader political system context; refine the statement of the problem, options and implementation considerations in light of health system and political system factors; anticipate monitoring and evaluation needs; and make national policy recommendations or decisions. The render crops the left edge, truncating the title and body text.
narratives.ar: الشكل 3، إطار التوجيهات المسندة بالبيّنات بشأن النظم الصحية لأغراض رسم السياسات: تسلسل رأسي من ثماني خطوات على شكل أسهم بدرجات البرتقالي، لكل منها شريط نصي رمادي: توضيح المشكلة؛ وصياغة الخيارات؛ وتحديد اعتبارات التنفيذ؛ ومراعاة السياق الأوسع للنظام الصحي؛ ومراعاة السياق الأوسع للنظام السياسي؛ وتنقيح بيان المشكلة والخيارات واعتبارات التنفيذ في ضوء عوامل النظام الصحي والنظام السياسي؛ وتوقع احتياجات الرصد والتقييم؛ واتخاذ توصيات أو قرارات وطنية بشأن السياسات. والحافة اليسرى مقصوصة، مما يبتر العنوان ونص المتن.
narratives.zh: 图3：基于证据的卫生系统决策指导框架：八个橙色系箭头形步骤纵向排列，每步配有灰色文字条：明确问题；提出备选方案；确定实施考虑因素；考虑更广泛的卫生系统背景；考虑更广泛的政治制度背景；根据卫生系统和政治制度因素完善对问题、方案和实施考虑因素的表述；预判监测和评价需求；提出国家政策建议或作出决定。图像左边缘被裁切，标题和正文不完整。
narratives.es: Figura 3, marco para la orientación sobre sistemas de salud basada en la evidencia para la formulación de políticas: secuencia vertical de ocho pasos en forma de galón en tonos naranja, cada uno con una barra de texto gris: aclarar el problema; plantear las opciones; determinar las consideraciones de aplicación; considerar el contexto más amplio del sistema de salud; considerar el contexto más amplio del sistema político; precisar el enunciado del problema, las opciones y las consideraciones de aplicación a la luz de los factores del sistema de salud y del sistema político; prever las necesidades de seguimiento y evaluación; y formular recomendaciones o decisiones normativas nacionales. La imagen está recortada por el borde izquierdo, lo que trunca el título y el texto.
narratives.fr: Figure 3, cadre pour des orientations sur les systèmes de santé fondées sur des données probantes à l'appui de l'élaboration des politiques : séquence verticale de huit étapes en forme de chevrons dans des tons orange, chacune accompagnée d'une barre de texte grise : clarifier le problème ; formuler les options ; recenser les éléments à prendre en compte pour la mise en œuvre ; examiner le contexte plus large du système de santé ; examiner le contexte plus large du système politique ; affiner l'énoncé du problème, des options et des éléments de mise en œuvre à la lumière des facteurs liés au système de santé et au système politique ; anticiper les besoins de suivi et d'évaluation ; et formuler des recommandations ou décisions politiques nationales. Le rendu est rogné sur le bord gauche, ce qui tronque le titre et le texte.
narratives.ru: Рисунок 3 — рамочная основа для основанных на фактических данных рекомендаций по системам здравоохранения в целях выработки политики: вертикальная последовательность из восьми шагов в виде шевронов оттенков оранжевого, каждый с серой текстовой полосой: уточнить проблему; сформулировать варианты; определить соображения по реализации; учесть более широкий контекст системы здравоохранения; учесть более широкий контекст политической системы; уточнить формулировку проблемы, вариантов и соображений по реализации с учётом факторов системы здравоохранения и политической системы; предусмотреть потребности в мониторинге и оценке; выработать национальные рекомендации или решения в области политики. Изображение обрезано по левому краю, из-за чего заголовок и основной текст неполны.
